meetings.title: Pricing working session: AI features
segments: Hi all. Aisha, are you there?
I see you but can't hear you.
Sorry, I was on mute. I'm here.
Classic.
Thanks for making time. Goal today is to agree on the proposal I take to leadership.
Helen, can you start with the cost model?
Sure. Using Priya's numbers, the median workspace costs about a dollar eighty a month in AI costs.
The largest is around fourteen dollars.
Almost all of it is theme summaries.
On our Pro price, that's fine for the median.
The risk is the tail, a few very large accounts.
How confident are those numbers?
If the model price changes, does everything move?
The numbers assume today's model pricing and today's usage.
Model prices have been going down, not up, so I think the risk is on usage, not price.
If customers use summaries far more than in the pilot, costs rise with them.
Which is exactly what a cap protects against.
So three options. A, include AI in Pro with a usage cap on summaries.
B, a separate AI add-on.
C, per-seat pricing like the competitor.
Please not C. Kestrel literally told us per-seat AI pricing was why they walked away from the competitor. Buyers hate it.
Did Kestrel say how the per-seat pricing was presented to them?
Fifteen dollars per seat per month, on top of the base plan, for everyone who can see the AI features.
For their sixty-person support team, that was more than the whole base contract.
Grace said it felt like being charged twice.
And per seat punishes exactly the behavior we want, which is more people looking at the themes.
That's a great line for the launch, honestly.
'AI for your whole team, not per seat.'
And from a positioning point of view, 'AI included in Pro' is a much stronger story than an add-on.
It says this is the product, not an upsell.
What about option B, the add-on?
Some companies do very well with that.
It adds a second negotiation to every deal.
Buyers who already have budget for us need to go find more budget for the AI part.
In my experience that slows deals down by weeks.
Financially, the add-on would bring in more revenue per account in the short term.
But if it slows deals and hurts retention, it's not worth it.
I'm persuaded by option A.
I'm fine with A, as long as the cap protects margin.
What cap works? At the alignment meeting I floated fifty thousand comments a month summarized in Pro.
What counts as a comment for the cap?
If a customer imports ninety days of history on day one, do they blow through it immediately?
Good catch. I'd exclude the initial backfill from the cap.
Otherwise the onboarding moment we're designing around becomes a pricing problem.
Yes, please. That would be a terrible first week.
Excluding the backfill is fine financially, it's a one-time cost.
I'll include it in the model as onboarding cost.
And duplicates? Some customers get the same comment from two sources.
We de-duplicate before summarizing anyway, so duplicates don't count twice.
I'll make that explicit in the proposal.
At fifty thousand, the worst case in Pro is about nine dollars a month in costs.
That keeps us above our eighty percent gross margin target on every Pro account.
Above the cap, accounts move to Business, which has room.
How many customers would actually hit fifty thousand comments a month today?
Using the pilot data and our current customer base, about four percent of Pro accounts.
Most of them are already close to the Business tier for other reasons.
So the cap is also a natural upgrade trigger.
Right, which is good, as long as it feels fair, not punishing.
What happens when someone hits the cap mid-month?
I don't want the feature to just stop working.
Good point. Clustering keeps working, since it's cheap.
Only new summaries pause, with a clear message and an upgrade path.
And we warn at eighty percent of the cap.
Should the cap reset monthly, or roll over?
Monthly reset. Rollover sounds generous, but it's confusing to explain and hard to forecast.
Simple beats clever for pricing.
Agreed. Simple is easier to put on a pricing page too.
That's a much friendlier experience.
Okay, so the proposal is option A.
AI included in Pro, summaries capped at fifty thousand comments a month, clustering unlimited, warning at eighty percent, Business uncapped. Everyone comfortable?
Yes.
Yes. I'd like to test the message with two or three prospects before it's final.
Please do, but don't quote prices. Just the shape.
I'll test the packaging shape with Kestrel and Juniper this week, no prices.
Which two will you start with?
Kestrel first, because Grace already told us what she hates about per-seat pricing.
Then Juniper, because they're the most price-sensitive prospect we have.
If the shape works for both of them, it'll work for most.
I'll run a sensitivity analysis on the cap, what if usage doubles next year.
What would make you uncomfortable in the sensitivity analysis?
What's the scenario you're worried about?
Two things. A few very large Pro accounts sitting just under the cap every month, which would squeeze margin without triggering an upgrade.
And summaries becoming so popular that median usage triples.
Neither is likely this year, but I want to know the numbers before we commit publicly.
If summaries become that popular, that's a good problem to have.
It is, as long as the price reflects it.
I'll bring both scenarios to the leadership review, with a recommendation for each.
That's perfect. Honestly, having the downside modeled will make Chris much more comfortable saying yes.
And if it helps, I can share what the prospects say about the shape before Helen finalizes anything.
If someone reacts badly to the cap, we'll know early.
Please do. Real reactions beat my assumptions every time.
I'll draft the packaging copy for the pricing page, so leadership sees how it reads.
Will the tier names change?
Pro and Business mean very little to buyers.
Not for this launch. Renaming tiers is a much bigger project, and it would distract from Insights.
I'd rather describe what each tier includes more clearly on the page.
Agreed. One change at a time.
And I'll write up the proposal for the leadership review.
Thanks all, this was fast.
Can the write-up include what we'd say to existing Pro customers?
They'll get AI features they didn't pay for, which is great, but they'll ask whether their price is changing.
Yes. The message is simple: nothing changes on your price, and you get Insights included, within the cap.
I'll put the exact wording in the proposal.
That's a nice message to send, honestly. Good news for once.
Maya, when's the leadership review?
I want to make sure I test the shape before it.
It's on the calendar for later this week.
So you have a few days.
Even two conversations would help.
I'll make it happen. Thanks, everyone.
